newsitem.title: USA: Key memo a document allowed in Fla. tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Key memo a document allowed in Fla. tobacco case.

text.p: One of the documents that a Florida judge ruled Tuesday could be used by plaintiffs in an upcoming secondhand smoke trial is a 1963 memo in which former Brown & Williamson general counsel Addison Yeaman indicated nicotine was an addictive drug.

Dade Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye issued a ruling Tuesday morning saying that document and 15 other confidential documents taken from a law firm working for Brown & Williamson, U.S. tobacco arm of B.A.T Industries Plc, could be used by plaintiffs' attorneys Stanley and Susan Rosenblatt in the class action suit by flight attendants.
Attorneys for Brown & Williamson had argued that the document should have been protected by attorney-client privilege.

The document was used last summer in another Florida tobacco case, which resulted in an Aug. 9 judgement in favor of Grady Carter of Orange Park, Fla. Lawyers for Brown & Williamson subsequently sought to overturn that judgment, claiming that internal company documents, including the 1963 memo, had been improperly used as evidence.
At Tuesday's hearing, Kaye also ruled that 12 of the Brown & Williamson documents the Rosenblatts had sought to use may not be used in the trial, to start June 2.
